entries.name: Svalbard reindeer
behaviour: endemic to Svalbard; found everywhere except the big glaciers, often on bare nunatak rock
sedentary all year: does not migrate, eats snow when water is locked
no land predators on Svalbard: humans and the sea are its only real hunters

voxel_model.pattern: sheds to grey-white in winter

entries.notes: The emblem of Svalbard's ice-free fringes: tiny, plump, long-haired and fearless. The only large land mammal in the North Atlantic high Arctic.

entries.name: Bowhead whale
entries.migrates: seasonal, follows the spring ice melt into leads and the autumn freeze back out
behaviour: breaks through half a metre of ice with its head to breathe in leads
V-shaped skim-feeding; needs to eat about 100 tonnes of zooplankton a year
longest baleen of any whale, up to 4.3 m, over 300 plates per side

voxel_model.pattern: black with white chin and tail markings on the old

entries.notes: The most ice-adapted baleen whale on Earth and, at two centuries, the oldest-lived mammal known: a stone harpoon fragment was recovered from one killed in 2007. The immovable giant of the small ice fields.

entries.name: King penguin
behaviour: egg brooded on the feet like the emperor; breeding cycle of 14-16 months, not yearly
vast dense colonies on flat subantarctic beaches; St Andrews Bay holds over 100,000 pairs
long crescent colonies read from the air as a dark carpet with moving rivers of birds

voxel_model.pattern: orange teardrop ear patches and throat

entries.notes: The second-largest penguin and the centrepiece of the subantarctic islands: the great orange-and-black crowds belong on the game's small-ice-cap coasts, not in Antarctica's interior.

entries.name: Atlantic puffin
behaviour: digs nesting burrows in seaside turf to escape the great black-backed gulls
carries fish crosswise in a deep scissor-like bill, up to a foot of sandeels at once
flies in low, stiff-winged whirr over breaking waves; spring congregation is chaotic

voxel_model.pattern: clown-striped bill, orange feet

entries.notes: The clown of Iceland: the biggest colonies on the coast around the small ice caps are millions of darting, burrowing, beak-ful puffins, with the razorbill as the striped supporting actor.

entries.name: Rock ptarmigan
entries.migrates: short altitudinal moves, following snow cover and forage
behaviour: Iceland's national bird; white in winter, mottled brown in summer
burrows into snowdrifts to roost through blizzards, like a living igloo
rooster holds a territory and courts with spread tail and raised crest

voxel_model.pattern: pure white in winter, barred brown in summer

entries.notes: The Icelandic 'rjúpa': an instantly recognisable bird of the snow-bare ridges that swap plumage with the seasons. A hardy, shuttling presence on the game's small bare summits.

entries.name: Snow bunting
entries.migrates: winters south of the snow line, forming huge swirling flocks
behaviour: breeds on bare nunataks poking out of the glacier edges and on rocky cliffs
digs a snow hollow for shelter when storms pin it down; the most northerly songbird
snow-white flashes in flocks on the first days of melt, arriving before the thaw

voxel_model.pattern: white wings and body, black wingtips, rusty nape

entries.notes: The little white and black streak on the nunatak ridge: the smallest warm heart of the glacier coast, and the first bird the player sees when the spring thaw begins.

entries.name: Arctic char
entries.migrates: anadromous, glacial lakes down to the fjords for summer
behaviour: runs up the meltwater rivers to spawn in autumn; the glacier-fed fish of the small ice caps
at sea it turns a salmon-red flank with the spawning season; back in the lake it silvers
feeds in the cold lakes under the ice edge where no other fish dares

voxel_model.pattern: red flanks and white-edged fins in spawning dress

entries.notes: The glacier lake fish: a firm, pink-fleshed salmonid that crosses the ice line in its lifetime. In-river fishing holes near the glacier front are the game's first cold-water rods.

entries.name: Barnacle goose
entries.migrates: long-distance flight from Svalbard to the Solway Firth and back each year
behaviour: nests on sheer cliff ledges hundreds of metres above the sea
goslings jump from the ledge days after hatching and free-fall to the grass below
was believed to hatch from goose barnacles, which is why it was eaten in Lent
sounds: higher, sharper yaps than the Canada goose

voxel_model.pattern: white face, black neck and chest, black-and-white wing bars

entries.notes: The black-and-white goose of the Svalbard cliffs: the gosling cliff-jump is the one animation that sells the whole species. Winter parties arrive over the UK like a flowing white-and-black ribbon.

entries.name: Common eider
entries.migrates: northern populations make long seasonal migrations, southern birds stay put
behaviour: the largest duck of the Northern Hemisphere, diving 20 m for shellfish
females pluck the warmest down off their own breasts to line the nest
Iceland 'eider farms' shelter nesting females to harvest the down

voxel_model.pattern: male: white back and dark belly; female: barred brown

entries.notes: The big heavy sea duck of the rocky fringe: tame, sociable and diving in ranked flocks, its down is worth money and Norwegian islanders made a living from it.

entries.name: Hooded seal
entries.migrates: whelps on the West Ice off Jan Mayen, winters in the Davis Strait and Greenland Sea
behaviour: males inflate a bright-red nasal septum balloon; the fastest wet-nurse of any mammal, pups weaned in 4 days
silver-grey adults with black faces and irregular dark blotches
dives to 1,000 m and stays under for almost an hour

voxel_model.pattern: silver-grey with dark blotches and a black face

entries.notes: The Jan Mayen ice-whelping giant: the inflating red hood display is the single most memorable sea-mammal animation on the small ice fields. A true West Ice speciality.

entries.name: Wandering albatross
entries.migrates: circumpolar, quartering the Southern Ocean on the mid-latitude westerlies
behaviour: the most far-reaching flier alive, soaring 1,000 km a day without flapping
monogamous with elaborate bill-circling partner dances; reunites after years apart
a chick lays down fat for a 1.5 kg weight gain between meals at sea

voxel_model.pattern: mostly white with black wing tips and a pale pink bill

entries.notes: The immense white ghost of the southern latitudes: a 3.5 m wingspan that needs no effort. A rare sight alongside the ice edge; one crossing the bow is reason enough to sail.

entries.name: Humpback whale
entries.migrates: long seasonal migrations, feeding at the ice edge, breeding in the tropics
behaviour: bubble-net feeding cooperatively at the krill swarms
haunting, years-long songs shared by all males of a breeding ground
white pectoral fins and notched flukes; breaches and tail-slaps endlessly

voxel_model.pattern: white flippers and knobbly head, pleated throat

entries.notes: The singing performer of the ice edge: bubble-nets, breaches and fluke slaps make it the whale a player will approach for a screenshot. Ice-edge humpbacks gorge before their long haul to warm water.

entries.name: Macaroni penguin
behaviour: grows an orange-yellow spiky brow crest with black-blue glossy back and white belly
largest of the crested penguins; populations at their Heard Island strongholds reach millions
forms vast jostling colonies that turn the beach yellow at hatching time

voxel_model.pattern: flaming yellow-orange brow crest

entries.notes: The flame-browed crested penguin: the sound of a million donkeys on a frozen black beach. In game terms the big subantarctic island coast should ring with this bird.

entries.name: Arctic tern
entries.migrates: pole-to-pole, chasing perpetual summer; the longest migration on Earth
behaviour: the most ambitious commuter alive: Arctic nest, Antarctic summer, back again each year
dives from a hovering stoop into the kelp line for sandeels
fiercely dive-bombs humans near the nest; razor-sharp screams over the sand spits

voxel_model.pattern: black cap, red bill, long tail streamers

entries.notes: The bird that owns both poles: its 80,000 km annual round trip crosses every route in the game. Any beach the player can walk on in the small ice-caps is guarded by this bird.

entries.name: Pink-footed goose
entries.migrates: Iceland and Svalbard to UK farmland, with big flocks descending in the dark
behaviour: winters in huge flocks on English and Scottish barley stubble, then streams up to the ice-free spits to breed
pink bill with dark tip and dark legs give the bird its name
a few hundred thousand come down to Britain every autumn

voxel_model.pattern: pink bill with dark tip, dark head and neck

entries.notes: The Icelandic/Svalbard breeder: in autumn the skies over the UK fill with a rolling gabble and the fields below come crawling with pink-legged grey geese.

entries.name: Northern fulmar
behaviour: nests on cliff ledges and nunataks; both light and dark morphs occur
vomits a burning spray of rancid stomach oil at anything that approaches the nest
wings held stiff, flaps a few times and then holds a rigid glide

voxel_model.pattern: light or dark morph; tubed yellow bill

entries.notes: The 'foul gull': a cliff bird that owns two colour forms and one unforgettable trick. If the player walks the scree below a ledge colony, a fountain of orange oil is a fair outcome.

entries.name: Great skua
entries.migrates: weakly migratory; disperses at sea in winter
behaviour: kleptoparasitise puffins, gulls and kittiwakes until they drop their catch
dive-bombs human heads near nests; aggressive to any moving thing on the ground
Iceland's Stórsúpa, the 'Icelandic falcon', also breeds on Bjørnøya

voxel_model.pattern: dark body, grizzled golden streaks above

entries.notes: The bonxie: Iceland's big dark pirate. A breeding pair on black sand will scream at the player from above before the warning dive; never skylark over a skua colony.

entries.name: Black guillemot
behaviour: pure black plumage in summer with a bright red gape, white wing flashes in flight
nests in crevices of the wave-cut basalt stacks; far more shy and hidden than the cliff-dwelling auks
winter turns white with fine black barring

voxel_model.pattern: summer: black with red gape; white wing flashes

entries.notes: The shy basalt-crevice black auk: the winter colour change is the give-away when snow is on the stacks. A low-key bird that populates every rocky notch off the ice fringe.

entries.name: Arctic cod
behaviour: the small fish that lives exactly under the sea ice; ices safe at -1.8 °C body fluids
forms vast schools beneath the fast ice, feeding on copepods
winter spawner; the food chain of the whole ice sheet hangs on this one fish

voxel_model.pattern: silvery flanks, dark back, three dorsal fins

entries.notes: The ice-sheet analogue of the antarctic silverfish: a few centimetres of food chain. Every ice-associated predator in this catalog ultimately depends on it.

entries.name: Capelin
entries.migrates: annual inshore spawning runs; Iceland names the run 'loðna'
behaviour: beaches erupt with spawning capelin in June: the whole fjord fills with migratory schools
males develop a ridged, torpedo-like edge of scales along the flank; females lay under the sand
Iceland and Norway fish huge quantities when the run announces itself

voxel_model.pattern: silvery sides, olive back, small weak stripe

entries.notes: The great Icelandic spawning fish: on the nights the run reaches the beach the whole coast feeds. A fishable tide the player can time their summer around.

entries.name: Common minke whale
entries.migrates: seasonal, spends summers at the ice edge and fjords
behaviour: the smallest baleen whale of the North Atlantic, and the boldest in showing its back
North Atlantic males sing a repeating 'boing' chorus
slick-backed arcs over the surface with a tall fluke on the dive

voxel_model.pattern: white flipper band, white chin

entries.notes: The northern 'little rorqual': ubiquitous in the ice-edge fjords and the star of every Icelandic whale-watch. Should be seen routinely off any small ice-cap coast.

entries.name: Grey seal
behaviour: horse-headed muzzle and pale, ant-like nostrils; the dullest face of any seal
hauls out on wave-washed rock; pups in white fur born in winter
Iceland-breeding grey seals weigh half as much as the North Seas bulls

voxel_model.pattern: horse-like muzzle, silver and dark-mottled coat

entries.notes: The rocky-shore seal of the Icelandic coast and Faroese stacks: not an ice seal, but the everyday pinniped of the small ice-cap fringe. Seen at every wet boulder landing.

entries.name: King eider
entries.migrates: seasonal sea-ice-edge migrations
behaviour: males: brilliant white wings, rusty nape, blue-green head shield, orange bill
dives to 30 m in the open high-Arctic sea, often in big feeding parties
the high-Arctic cousin of the common eider, breeding further north on bare rock

voxel_model.pattern: drake: white wings, rusty nape, green shield

entries.notes: The high-Arctic eider: the drake's gaudy white, rust and green is the most colourful thing on the bleak ridge-top breeding ground where it nests.

entries.name: Long-tailed duck
entries.migrates: long irruptive migrations; winters on open leads in the pack ice
behaviour: dives to 60 m, holds its breath for over three minutes, eating crustaceans on the bottom
males: extravagant white crest, black head with a white cheek crescent and two long tail plumes
winter flocks are enormous; the North Atlantic opens up in long streams

voxel_model.pattern: black head, white cheek crescent, trailing tail plumes

entries.notes: The sea duck of the open leads: pure joy of design, all crest and plumes, singing its yodel over the pack ice well into the freeze.

entries.name: Purple sandpiper
entries.migrates: short-distance, wintering on the northern shores
behaviour: breeds on high-Arctic stony flats and moor, winters in seaweed on the rockiest surf
purple-bronze sheen in the sun; orange legs and bill base
the one wader that winters on the ice-battered coastline, beat the waves for limpets

voxel_model.pattern: purple-bronze above, pale wing flash, orange legs

entries.notes: The shore wader of the very edge: a sandpiper for the war of the waves, working the seaweed with the surf at its back. Pure sea-spray wildlife.

entries.name: Brent goose
entries.migrates: breeds on Arctic coasts, winters on northern estuaries in huge ribbons
behaviour: famously eats eelgrass; Brent geese were starving when Spartina spread began to replace it
black neck and chest, white stern, dark and pale morphs in both races
a migration of tens of thousands comes screaming down the estuary in autumn
sounds: low barking honks, softer than the Canada goose

voxel_model.pattern: black neck and stern, white stern patch; dark and pale morphs

entries.notes: The goose of the tidal flats: black-bellied and unforgettable in the winter mud, sweeping in from the Arctic in cones of honking wings.

entries.name: Harbour porpoise
behaviour: the smallest cetacean of the North Atlantic; small dark dorsal fin, rounded head, no beak
emits high-pitched clicks beyond the edge of human hearing
surfaces with a quick snort and is gone; 'puffing pig' was the sailor name

voxel_model.pattern: dark back, pale flank stripe, pale belly

entries.notes: The little dark cetacean of the ice-fringe harbour: a split-second fin in the kelp fringes off Iceland's small ice caps, heard as clicks before it is seen.

entries.name: Arctic skua
entries.migrates: long-distance migrant to southern oceans
behaviour: pirates the terns, kittiwakes and puffins at the ice edge, harassing them until they drop their catch
light and dark morphs both occur; the long central tail streamers are the deepest
roosts and breeds on the empty moor with the waders

voxel_model.pattern: dark cap, white cheek flashes; light and dark morphs

entries.notes: The little pirate of the north: smaller than its colonies suggest, brutal in the chase. Look for the wedge of tail streamers behind a tern the moment food appears.

entries.name: Southern rockhopper penguin
behaviour: rockhops ashore by bounding leaps up the wave-cut kelp lines
scarlet eyes, spiky yellow crest, spiky yellow eyebrows
nests in tussock grass; populations falling fast on Falklands and South Georgia

voxel_model.pattern: yellow spiky crest and eyebrow flashes, red eyes

entries.notes: The little rock-jumping crested penguin of the far south: the Falklands and South Georgia get a different coast altogether when this bird arrives, hopping up the sea's steps.

entries.name: Southern giant petrel
entries.migrates: disperses at sea in the south in the off-season
behaviour: the largest petrel alive; hunchbacked, macho and mostly dark or mostly white
scavenges the bodies of seals and penguins, and kills live chicks in the colonies
smells carrion from kilometres away; the vulture of the south ocean beaches

voxel_model.pattern: two morphs, dark and near-white; dark bill tip

entries.notes: The stinkpot: the dark hunchbacked vulture working the shore above the elephant seals. In-game it is the scavenger every big colony needs a few of.

entries.name: Greenland halibut
behaviour: a deep-water flatfish of 500-1000 m beneath the Arctic ice; both sides pigmented
swims vertically with a muscular, torpedo body far from the seabed
the top fisheries target of the northern small-ice fishery; often called 'turbot' on menus

voxel_model.pattern: dark on both sides, elongated oval body

entries.notes: The deep, dark, double-sided flatfish of the ice-sheet fjords: a cold-water game fish for long-line or cod pot, and the Inuit's treasure at the fjord bottom.

entries.name: Brown skua
behaviour: skua of the Falklands, Tristan and South Georgia; descends directly onto penguin colonies
attacks researchers who pass the territory; the southern twin of the Icelandic bird
all brown, with a white wing flash in the hand

voxel_model.pattern: dark overall, pale flash at base of the primaries

entries.notes: The South Atlantic's own skua: brown in the tussock grass of Falklands and South Georgia, patrolling the chick colonies when the albatross chicks go in the open.

entries.name: Cape petrel
entries.migrates: disperses at sea beyond the ice edge in winter
behaviour: checkerboard black-and-white pattern, white above with black spotting; 'pintado' in Spanish
one of the commonest birds of the Southern Ocean; huge flocks follow ships and feeding whales
nests in crevices of ice-free rock in the colonies of other seabirds

voxel_model.pattern: black-and-white checkerboard

entries.notes: The pintado: a speckled runner in the rigging of every sail-boat that has worked the ice. Its black-and-white chessboard wings are unmistakable at the feeding swarms.

entries.name: Glacier ice worm
entries.migrates: nightly vertical migration into and out of the glacier
behaviour: the only annelid to live permanently in glacier ice; a dark thread-like earthworm of the snowline
emerges at dusk to graze snow algae, burrows back into the ice at dawn
populations of tens of millions on a single coastal glacier, but dies above 7 °C
entries.notes: The only glacier-obligé worm on Earth: unfindable by day, countless by dusk on the Pacific Northwest glaciers. The single most improbable creature a small ice-cap cave could hide.

entries.name: Lion's mane jellyfish
behaviour: the largest jellyfish on Earth: bell up to 2 m across and tentacles trailing 30 m+
red-brown mass of stinging tentacles; swarms drift with the cold current
the long trailing tentacles are the cause of the worst sting on a North Atlantic beach

voxel_model.pattern: red bell, dark-red trailing tentacles

entries.notes: The great red medusa of the cold current: too big to miss and too bad to touch. A glowing red-orange mass drifting under the pier is a sign of the Arctic fringe at its most exotic.
